content: Potassium lactate is a chemical compound with the molecular formula KC3H5O3, also written as H3C-CHOH-COOK. It is the potassium salt derived from lactic acid. This compound is synthesized by neutralizing lactic acid, which itself is obtained through the fermentation of a sugar source. Potassium lactate is assigned the E number E326 in food additive classifications. Typically, potassium lactate is available as a liquid solution containing approximately 60% solids, although more concentrated forms with up to 78% solids are also commercially available. It is widely utilized in the food industry, particularly in meat and poultry products, due to its ability to extend shelf life and enhance food safety. This is achieved through its broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties, which effectively inhibit the growth of most spoilage organisms and pathogenic bacteria. In addition to its applications in the food industry, potassium lactate is also employed as an extinguishing agent. For example, it is a key component in the First Alert Tundra fire extinguishers, where it serves as a fire suppression medium.
